unfinished.reason: Mine to write, and I did not ship it: measured, the naive version reports 15 findings on a correct tree, all inside self-test fixtures. Shipping a check that fires on correct code is how a check gets weakened the first time it is wrong.
unfinished.detail: NO CHECK FAILS UNTIL THIS LANDS, and that is the point: six false citations were repaired in tests/ this round and nothing in the suite could see any of them, including the one inside O11's printed verdict. THE SHAPE THAT WOULD WORK: in check_o13_citations_resolve, add tests/**/*.py to `sources` (it is already walked to build `defined`), and skip any citation whose character offset falls inside a module-level string constant -- every fixture in tests/test_ownership.py and tests/test_contract.py is a `_NAME = '''...'''` or `_NAME = """..."""` assignment, and the 15 unresolvable citations are all inside one. The exemption is computable from the AST that check already has for tests/ files: collect (lineno, end_lineno) of every ast.Constant string that is the value of a module-level Assign, and drop citations on those lines. MEASURE BEFORE SHIPPING: with the exemption the count over both files must be 0, and a case pair belongs with it -- a fixture containing a false citation must stay ADMITTED while the same citation in a docstring must FAIL. I did not have room to calibrate that inside this round without risking the thing the round is about.

unfinished.title: tests/test_contract.py -- the 6 computed-reachability gates rule 4 still cannot judge
unfinished.reason: Deliberately left. Judging them means deciding that `floor_reachable` and `not sched_live` are the same condition, which is inference, and this file has a measurement for what inference costs.
unfinished.detail: NO CHECK FAILS. 9 of 15 are judged; the report line prints the split so the size of the residue is on the output rather than in a docstring. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT HONESTLY is not a more forgiving text comparison -- I measured the cheapest one (stripping `bool(...)`) and it gains zero gates on all 37 trees -- but a local const-propagation of the enclosing function's boolean assignments, so `floor_reachable = not sched_live` is resolved through _k15_assignments the way rule 3 already resolves value provenance. That is a real change with a real false-positive surface and it needs its own 37-tree sweep. The alternative, and probably the better one, is a CONVENTION: a dynamic gate's reason branches on the expression passed to `reachable=` and on nothing else, which would make all 15 judgeable and is a one-line rule in the same check. That is the owner's call, not mine.

unfinished.detail: NO CHECK FAILS, and the residue is strictly smaller than the one it replaces: the whole of src/spine/ was exempt until this round, and now only derive.py and assemble.py are. WHAT IS STILL UNSEEN is arithmetic hand-written in assemble.py OUTSIDE a COUPLINGS `compute` -- in a helper, say. THE NARROWER RULE, if anyone wants it: exempt a BinOp in assemble.py only when it is inside a Lambda that is the `compute=` keyword of a `Coupling(...)` call, and exempt the textual half only inside a `why=` string of one. I measured what the current exemption is worth: without it, the three O11 changes report four findings in assemble.py, at :1149 (OPT.d_effective_batch_windows' compute, two clock levers multiplied), :1012 (SIG.d_idle_cadence's compute) and :1020 (that row's own `why`, quoting the formula the compute performs) -- all four correctly declared couplings, all four already checked one at a time by tests/test_couplings.py::check_c1_legitimate_admitted and tests/test_couplings.py::check_c4_table_resolves.
